IS ; 10457 - 1983 



Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
N-METHYL-J-ACID 



0. FOREWORD 

0*1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 10 February 1983, after the draft finalized by the Dye 
Intermediates Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, 
Coal and Related Products Division Council. 

0,2 N-methyl-J-acid ( Cii Hn NO4S ) is an important dyo intermediate 
used for the manufacture of reactive dycstufis. The product is available 
in the form of the free acid. It is also known as 2-inethylamino-5- 
naphthol-7-sulphonic acid. It is represented by the following structural 
formula: 



HO1 




NH- 



•CH, 



OH 
N-METHYL-J-ACID 

( Molecular Mass 253*3 ) 

0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accord- 
ance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in 
the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value 
in this standard. 



^Rules for rounding off numerical values ( rms9d ). 



IS : 10457 - 1983 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of 
sampling and test for N-methyl-J-acid. 

2. REQUIREMENTS 

2*1 Description — The material shall be in the form of grey yellowish- 
brown powder or paste. 

2.2 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in 
Table 1.

3, PACKING AND MARKING 

3.1 Packing — The material shall be packed in 100-kg packing in steel 
drums ( see IS : 2552-1979* ) lined with suitable polyethylene film or as 
agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. Each container shall 
be securely closed. 



♦Specification for steel drums ( galvanized and ungalvanizcd ) ( second reiision ), 

4 



IS : 10457 - 1983 

3.2 Marking — Each container shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following informatioii: 

a) Name of the material; 

b) Name of the manufacturer and his recognized trade-mark, if 
any; 

c) Batch number; and 

d) Tare, net and gross mass. 

3.2.1 The containers may also be marked with the I SI Certification 
Mark. 

NoTK — Tho use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of 
the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regu- 
lations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the require- 
ments of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality 
control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI 
marked products are also continuously checked l>y ISI for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, 
may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution. 

4. SAMPLING 

4.1 Representative samples of the material shall be drawn as persrriV^ed 
in 3 of IS : 5299-1969*. 

4.2 Number of Tests 

4.2.1 Assay content shall be tested on each of the individual samples. 

4.2.2 The remaining requirements given in 2 of the specification shall 
be tested on the composite sample. 

4.3 Criteria for Conformity 

4.3.1 The lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of 
this standard if all the trst results on each of the individual samples and 
the composite sample meet the requirements given in 2. 

5. METHOD OF TESTS 

5.1 Tests shall be carried out according to the methods prescribed in 
Appendix A and IS : 5209-1969*. Reference to relevant clauses is given 
in col 4 and 5 of Table 1. 

5.2 Quality of Reagents — Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals 
an 1 distilled water ( see IS : 1070-1977f ) shall be employed in tests. 

Notf: — ' Pure chemicals ' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities 
which iiiTcct tho results of analysis.

APPENDIX A 

( Table 1, and Clause 5.1 ) 

METHOD OF TESTS FOR N-METHYL-J-ACID 

A-L DETERMINATION OF ASSAY 

A*1«0 General — The two methods for determining N-methyl-J-acid 
which are based on couphng value and by nitrosation are given below. 

A-1.1 Method A ( Based on Coupling Value ) 

A-1.1.1 Reagents 

A-Ll.1.1 Sodium carbonate solution — 1 M. 

A-1,1,1.2 p'Chlorobenzene diazonium chloride — 0*1 N. 

A-1.L1.3 Filter paper — Whatman No. 1. 

A-l.l*2 Procedure 

A-1.1,2.1 Weigh accurately 25 to 30 g of the thoroughly mixed 
paste sample ( 20 to 25 g if in powder form ) into a 1-litre beaker and 
add 200 ml water and sufficient 1 M sodium carbonate solution to make 
the solution alkaline to brilliant yellow paper. Boil for a few minutes 
and filter the hot solution through Whatman No. I filter paper. Wash 
with hot water until free from alkali. 

A-1.1.2.2 Cool the filtrate and washings and transfer to 1 -litre 
volumetric flask. Dilute to the mark with water and mix well. 

A*l.l*2.3 Pipette 50 ml of this solution into a 500-ml beaker, dilute 
to 200 ml with water, and add 5 g of sodium carbonate. Cool externally 
in a bath of ice and water, stir mechanically and titrate with 0* 1 N 
^-chlorobenzene diazonium chloride. Add 0*5 ml at a time towards the 
end of the titration. The end point is reached when a clear rim round 
a drop of the solution spotted on filter paper just fails to give a colour 
with the diazo solution five minutes after the last addition of the 
titraut 

A-1.1.3 Calculation 

Assay ( by coupling value ), 
( calculated as N-methyl-J-acid ) 
( molecular mass 253'3 ), V x N x 506*6 
percent by mass =» j-z 

where 

V aa volume in ml of /^-chlorobenzene diazonium chloride 
solution; 



IS : 10457 - 1983 

M = mass in g of the sample taken; and 

JV =• normality of /?-chlorobenzene diazonium chloride 
solution^ 

A.1.2 Method B ( by Nitrosation ) 

A-1,2J Procedure — Pipette 50 ml of the above solution ( see A-1.1.2.2 ) 
into a 500-ml beaker. Add 50 ml of concontrated hydrochloric acid 
followed by about 100 ml of water. Boil for about 10 minutes. Cool 
externally to about 5*^0 and titrate against 0*25 N sodium nitrite solution 
using starch iodide paper to detect the end point. 

A-1,2.2 Calculation 

Assay ( by nitrosation ), V x N X 506 6 
percent by mass » v/ -— 

where 

V =s volume in ml of sodium nitrite solution consumed; 
JV* =r normality of sodium nitrite solution; and 
M = mass in g of the sample taken. 

A-2. DETERMINATION OF J-ACID AND DI-J-ACID BY PAPER 
CHROMATOGRAPHY 

A-2*l Reagents 

A-2.1.1 n-Propanol — distilled. 

A-2. 1.2 Sulphanilic Acid 

A-2.1.3 Ammonia Solution — 25 percent ( vfv ). 

A-2.1.4 Whatman Paper — 3 mm thickness. 

A-2.1.5 Sodium Nitrite Solution — 1 N. 

A-2.1.6 Hydrochloric Acid — 1 M. 

A-2.1.7 Standard J-Acid Solution 

A.2.1.8 Solvent Mixtures — developing solvents ( ^-propanol and water 
in 70:30 ratio ). 

A-2«l«9 Sodium Acetate — crystalline. 

A-2.1.10 Sodium Hydroxide — IN. 

A-2.2 Apparatus 

A*2.2.1 Chromatographic Tank — Size 27 X 40 cm. 

7 



IS : 10457 . 1983 

A-2.2.2 Sprayer 

A-2.2.3 Ultra Violet Lamp 

A-2.3 Preparation of Solution 

A-2.3.1 Standard Sample Solution — Weigh exactly 10 ^ sample, dissolve 
in ammonia solution and make up to 100 ml with distilled water. 

A*2*3.2 Standard J-Acid Solution — Weigh 1 g of the material, dissolve 
in ammonia solution and make up to 100 ml with distilled water. From 
this pipette out 2'0 ml, 4*0 ml and 6*0 ml in three 100-ml measuring 
flasks and make up to mark with water. Call these solutions A, B and C 
respectively. 

A<-2.3.3 Standard Di-J Acid Solution — Weigh 1 g of the material, 
dissolve in ammonia solution and make up to 100 ml with distilled water. 
From this pipette out 1*0 ml, 20 ml and 3'0 ml in three 100-ml measur- 
ing flasks and make up to mark with water. Call these solution A^ B 
and C respectively. 

A-2.4 Spots 

A-2.4.1 Sample Solution — O'Ol ml = 100 micrograms. 
A-2.4.2 J-Acid Solution 

O-Ol ml ( /i ) = 2 percent 
O'Ol ml ( J5 ) = 4 pen ent 
0-01 ml ( C) = 6 percent 

A-2.4.3 Di-J-Acid Solution 

0*01 ml ( ^ ) «» 1 percent 
0-0 1 ml ( ^ ) = 2 percent 
001 ml ( C) « 3 percent 

A-2.5 Technique — Ascend ing paper chromatography. 

A-2.6 Preparation of Tank 

A»2,6.1 Place 200*0 nil of developing mixture into the chromato- 
graphic tank and replace the lid. Allow to equilibrate for about an 
hour. 

A-2.7 Development of Ghromatogram 

A-2.7.1 After spotting, suspend the paper from the supporting rods by 
means of clips so that a lower edge of the paper is jnst touching the 
surface of the developing solvent but does not touch the bottom of the 
tank. Allow the chrornatogram to develop for about 16 hours. After 

8 



IS : 10457 . 1983 

developing and drying at 100°C for 10 minutes, develop fluorescence by 
holding the paper over a beaker containing concentrated ammonium 
hydroxide solution ( 25 percent ). When the paper is examined under 
a ultra violet lamp the following fluorescence are seen: 

i) strong bhie fluorescence of N-mcthyl-J-acid ( main band ) at the 
top; and 

ii) light blue fluorescence of J-acid in the middle. 

A-2.7.2 Further assessment shall be made as under. 

A«2«7,2*l The chromatogram is coupled by spraying 01 N benzene 
diazonium chloride-4-suiphonic acid. It is prepared as follows: 

Weigh approximately 1*7 g of sulphanilic acid add 15 ml of 1 N 
sodium hydroxide solution to dissolve and add 30 to 40 ml of 1 M 
hydrochloric acid, 30 ml of water and cool to 5°C. To this add 
previously cooled 10*0 ml of 1 N sodium nitrite solution. Mix well and 
make up to 100 ml with cold water. The resultant diazo solution should 
give immediate blue colouration when spotted on a starch iodide paper. 
Add 5 g of crystalline sodium acetate to the above solution. 

A-2.8 Results 

A-2,8.1 The following chromatogram develops: 



i) CRIMSON PeO COLOUR 
BAND OF N-METHYL- 
J-ACIO AT TH6 TOP 



ii) DULL RED COLOUR 
BAND OF J- ACID 
IN THE MIDDLE 

ill) PURPLE BAND OF 
DhJ-ACiD 



IV) IMPURITIES REGIOK 
AT THE BOTTOM 



V) SPOT

and Di-J-acid contents.
